utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is case IT-04-74-T, Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. We are the 25th of April, 2007. I'd like to greet all the people present in the courtroom, the OTP representatives, Defence counsel, and the accused. From what I understood, somebody wanted to take the floor this morning, I believe. Mr. Stewart or Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I was trying to signal. We do have a problem with our computer. I'm sorry to interrupt. I was just trying to signal to the officers in question that Ms. Alaburic has a problem. My apologies if it was directed in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone. Just a couple of minor points. One, we would like either the Trial Chamber, or I could do so, to inquire from the witness before he testifies today whether overnight he consulted his statement. I don't -- did not ask for a protective measure last night, that is for him -- to prevent him from looking at his statement and refreshing his memory overnight or memorising his statement, given that it would appear that he has no recollection of many of the events or at least the quotations that he wishes to -- to use from his -- his statement. So I would ask that he -- that an inquiry be made as to whether he read his statement, because if that is the case, then again I would renew my request that he be disallowed to testify any further, because then again the testimony that we would hear today would be based on a memory that has been prepped and perhaps even provoked, as I would say, by -- by reading his -- his statement, and it would not be an independent recollection. So that's the first. Another matter which I would raise at this point for the Court to consider - perhaps during the break you can convene - is in light of my earlier request yesterday to do a voir dire and, given the time limitations, I would respectfully request on behalf of everybody that we be allotted 30 extra minutes for one of us to delve into those issues, that is the issues of how the statement was prepared, to what extent he relied on his notes, what notes he relied on, what documents he gave to the Prosecution concretely. We would like to hear it from the witness himself so we could have an adequate record upon which later on we could renew our request that the testimony be disallowed since the Trial Chamber indicated that it was premature to have made that decision yesterday. That's it, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to say we, Mr. Karnavas and I, have discussed this. We fully support that. Your Honour, we don't have in mind, of course, that we would duplicate our examination on that issue, but we do strongly urge that 30 minutes is a sensible estimate of the extra time needed for that discreet matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think probably it would be better if we'd been in private session. If we could go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 26th day of April, 2007, at 2007 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
